column8: Saurabh: We have been stressing too much on quantity of goals rather than quality and purpose. We keep setting unrealistic and unachievable goals to show that we are ambitious but end up demotivating the team. We should set fewer goals which are SMART, aligned and motivational rather than too many random and directionless goals.
column9: Priyanka: I agree we have gone overboard with number of goals but we also need to be aggressive to achieve our key targets and set the right example.We should set combination of long term visionary goals along with short term tactical goals.We must get the timing and complexity right so that  people feel motivated and not overwhelmed.Frequent feedback and course correction will help.
column10: Gaurabv: You both have valid points. As managers, we need to strike a balance between motivation and realism.Our goals should be challenging yet achievable.We must provide clarity of purpose and enough flexibility for teams to experiment.Rather than criticising people for missing goals, we should review if the goals were appropriate and realistic.We should set the right environment for people to thrive and grow while achieving key results.

column2: This is a random watercooler discussion between the employees and their managers about Goal setting in the department. Its a open and frank conversation with few formalities. Anuv, Saumya, Vikramaditya,  and the employees with their own challenges and thoughts about the Goal setting in the department. This is a Operations Department in a Power Distribution Sector. Create a opening conversation with comments from Anuv(Production Engineer), Saumya(Project Supervisor), Vikramaditya(Project Surveyor), . Their manager will soon join them.
column8: Anuv: As the Production Engineer, my team faces a lot of challenges in achieving the production targets set for us in the department. The targets seem unrealistic at times and do not factor in the difficulties involved in streamlining the production processes. My team needs to be provided realistic and concrete goals which they can work towards rather than vague production numbers. Only then will they feel motivated and committed to achieving them.
column9: Saumya: Being the Project Supervisor, I have noticed that my team struggles when the project goals are not clearly defined. They work best when provided with precise deadlines and quantifiable targets. If the goals are ambiguous, it leads to confusion and hampers productivity. My team needs clear guidelines to work efficiently and achieve the desired results. Setting unambiguous and measurable goals is key to the success of any project.
column10: Vikramaditya: As the Project Surveyor, I have observed that my team's motivation levels fluctuate based on the complexity of the tasks assigned to them. When faced with overly complicated projects, their morale and dedication tend to drop. For the team to feel motivated, the goals must be challenging yet achievable given their skills and abilities. If the targets are beyond their capabilities, it can lead to frustration and negatively impact their performance. Realistic expectations are important to keep the team motivated.
